summary: Iteration_7 verifies the NEW STRICT designation filter on /api/oem-stock-search. 16 tests written (9 helper unit, 5 regression, 3 live endpoint). 15/16 PASS. The filter logic is provably CORRECT: helpers `_designation_query_tokens` and `_designation_has_all_tokens` behave exactly as specified, and the filter wiring in the response builder (server.py L1458-1460) drops every item whose designation lacks any required token. The single failing test (test_kit_chaine_distribution_strict) is a DATA REALITY issue, NOT a filter bug: direct MongoDB inspection of supplier_lookup_cache shows the entire warm cache contains 11 items with 'kit', 5 with 'chaine', and only 1 with 'distribution' — and ZERO items where all three words co-occur. Suppliers use abbreviations like 'KIT DIST' (no 'DISTRIBUTION'/no 'CHAINE') or 'CHAINE DISTRIBUTION 1.6 HDI' (no 'KIT'). The two-token query q='chaine,distribution' DOES return count=1 ('CHAINE DISTRIBUTION 1.6 HDI'), proving the filter is correctly wired end-to-end and the architectural fixes from iter_6 (partial-results loop, PA_COMPAT_CAP=50, FadPro variant fallback) are all still active.

minor.issue: STRICT filter returns count=0 because no supplier item in the entire warm cache contains all 3 of 'kit'+'chaine'+'distribution' together. Direct DB scan: 11 items contain 'kit' (all 'KIT DIST...' or 'KIT CHAINE ARBRE A CAMES...'), 5 contain 'chaine', only 1 contains 'distribution' ('CHAINE DISTRIBUTION 1.6 HDI' — no 'kit'), 0 contain all three. The filter is operating correctly; the supplier catalog simply does not contain any item whose human-written designation spells out 'KIT CHAINE DISTRIBUTION' literally. Suppliers abbreviate.

action_items: CRITICAL DECISION FOR MAIN AGENT: The strict filter is mathematically correct but produces count=0 for q='Kit,chaine,distribution' because suppliers use abbreviations. Two non-mocking options to recover items: (a) Add a synonym map at filter time so 'distribution' also matches 'dist', and treat 'kit chaine' as a positive match if the candidate OEM was originally tagged in the chaine/distribution sub-category in piecesautos.tn compat scraping. (b) Apply the strict filter ONLY when q has >= 3 tokens AND at least one returned item passes; otherwise fall back to >=2 of N tokens. Recommend (a) — add `{'distribution': ['distribution','dist'], 'chaine': ['chaine','chn']}` synonym expansion to _designation_has_all_tokens, since user clearly wants the KIT DIST POMPE A EAU items to appear under 'kit chaine distribution'.

OPTIONAL: Consider also matching against the OEM reference, not just the designation, OR matching against the upstream piecesautos.tn category label that was used to pick this OEM — the OEM IS in the chaine-distribution sub-cat by upstream classification; only the human-written supplier label disagrees.

OPTIONAL: 2-token query 'chaine,distribution' returning count=1 ('CHAINE DISTRIBUTION 1.6 HDI') proves the filter wiring is correct; the issue is purely semantic-mismatch between the sub-cat label 'Kit chaine distribution' and supplier-written designations that abbreviate.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L377-417 the two helpers are pure (no I/O), correctly use unicodedata.NFKD + combining-character strip for accent normalisation, and the regex `[a-z0-9]{3,}` correctly drops short stopwords without a hard-coded list.

server.py L1458-1460 the filter is applied AFTER the supplier gather and BEFORE the sort, in the response builder — placement is correct (filtering before sort avoids wasting sort cycles on doomed items). The filter is O(n*|tokens|*|designation|) per request which is negligible at n<=1000.

POTENTIAL ENHANCEMENT (not a bug): the substring test `t in norm` will match overlapping tokens (e.g., 'kit' also matches inside 'kitchen', though irrelevant for auto parts). Consider word-boundary regex `\b{t}\b` if false-positive precision matters.

POTENTIAL ENHANCEMENT: the helper does not handle synonyms or abbreviations. Real-world supplier data uses 'DIST' for 'DISTRIBUTION', 'POMPE A EAU' instead of 'POMPE-EAU', etc. A small synonym table per sub-cat would dramatically improve recall without sacrificing precision.

rca_of_the_issue: OBSERVATION: q='Kit,chaine,distribution' → HTTP 200 / count=0 / 40.23s; user requested count >= 1. DIAGNOSIS: filter implementation is correct; problem is semantic mismatch between sub-category label and supplier-written designation strings. EVIDENCE: direct MongoDB scan of supplier_lookup_cache shows 11 items with 'kit' (all 'KIT DIST...'), 5 with 'chaine', 1 with 'distribution' ('CHAINE DISTRIBUTION 1.6 HDI', which lacks 'kit'), 0 items containing all three words simultaneously. PROOF FILTER WIRING IS CORRECT: q='chaine,distribution' returns count=1 with designation 'CHAINE DISTRIBUTION 1.6 HDI'. ROOT CAUSE: suppliers abbreviate 'DISTRIBUTION' to 'DIST' and write 'KIT DIST' or 'CHAINE DISTRIBUTION' but never spell out 'KIT CHAINE DISTRIBUTION' together. MITIGATION OPTIONS for main agent: (1) add a token-synonym map ({'distribution':['distribution','dist']}) inside _designation_has_all_tokens — recommended, restores ~11 KIT DIST items into results; (2) relax to 'at least N-1 of N tokens must match' when N>=3; (3) accept that count=0 is the literally-correct answer and document in UI ('No exact match — try removing a word').
